name: Stephen King
aboutText: Stephen King is an American author of horror and supernatural fiction. His books have sold more than 350 million copies worldwide and many have been adapted into films.

name: Agatha Christie
aboutText: Agatha Christie was an English mystery writer and the best-selling fiction writer of all time. Her detective novels featuring Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple have captivated readers for over a century.

name: J.K. Rowling
aboutText: J.K. Rowling is a British author best known for the Harry Potter fantasy series. The series has sold over 500 million copies worldwide and has been adapted into a highly successful film series.

name: Haruki Murakami
aboutText: Haruki Murakami is a Japanese novelist whose works blend magical realism with pop culture and loneliness. His novels Norwegian Wood and Kafka on the Shore have captivated millions of readers worldwide.

name: George Orwell
aboutText: George Orwell was an English novelist whose works 1984 and Animal Farm remain among the most influential books ever written. His ideas about totalitarianism shaped modern political thought.

name: Toni Morrison
aboutTitle: Voice of the African American Experience
aboutText: Toni Morrison was an American novelist and Nobel Prize winner. Her novel Beloved is considered one of the most powerful works in American literature.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
aboutText: Gabriel García Márquez was a Colombian novelist and Nobel Prize winner. His novel One Hundred Years of Solitude defined magical realism and sold over 50 million copies worldwide.

name: Franz Kafka
aboutText: Franz Kafka was a German-speaking Bohemian novelist whose works The Metamorphosis and The Trial explore themes of alienation and existential dread.

name: Virginia Woolf
aboutText: Virginia Woolf was an English writer considered one of the most important modernist literary figures of the 20th century. Her novels Mrs Dalloway and To the Lighthouse revolutionized narrative technique.

name: Ernest Hemingway
aboutText: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist and Nobel Prize winner known for his economical writing style. His works The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms are classics of American literature.

name: Jane Austen
aboutText: Jane Austen was an English novelist known for her sharp social commentary and wit. Her novels Pride and Prejudice and Emma are beloved classics read by millions worldwide.

name: Charles Dickens
aboutText: Charles Dickens was an English novelist and social critic who created some of the most memorable characters in literature. His works A Tale of Two Cities and Great Expectations are timeless classics.

name: Leo Tolstoy
aboutText: Leo Tolstoy was a Russian writer widely regarded as one of the greatest novelists of all time. His masterpieces War and Peace and Anna Karenina represent the pinnacle of realist fiction.

name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
aboutText: Fyodor Dostoevsky was a Russian novelist whose works explore human psychology and redemption. His novels Crime and Punishment and The Brothers Karamazov are among the greatest ever written.

name: Oscar Wilde
aboutText: Oscar Wilde was an Irish poet and playwright known for his brilliant wit. His novel The Picture of Dorian Gray and his play The Importance of Being Earnest are enduring classics.

name: Albert Camus
aboutText: Albert Camus was a French-Algerian novelist and Nobel Prize winner. His works The Stranger and The Plague explore themes of absurdism and the human condition.

name: Victor Hugo
aboutText: Victor Hugo was a French poet and novelist whose works Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame are among the most celebrated novels in history.

name: Dante Alighieri
aboutText: Dante Alighieri was an Italian poet whose Divine Comedy is widely considered the greatest literary work composed in Italian and one of the greatest works of world literature.

name: Homer
aboutText: Homer was an ancient Greek poet credited with composing the Iliad and the Odyssey, the two foundational works of Western literature.

name: William Shakespeare
aboutTitle: The Greatest Writer of All Time
aboutText: William Shakespeare was an English playwright widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language. His works including Hamlet and Romeo and Juliet have influenced literature for 400 years.

name: Marcel Proust
aboutText: Marcel Proust was a French novelist best known for his monumental work In Search of Lost Time, widely considered one of the greatest achievements in all of literature.

name: Jorge Luis Borges
aboutText: Jorge Luis Borges was an Argentine short-story writer whose works explore themes of infinity, mirrors, and reality. He is considered one of the most influential writers of the 20th century.

name: Gustave Flaubert
aboutText: Gustave Flaubert was a French novelist widely considered the greatest Western novelist. His novel Madame Bovary revolutionized literary realism.

name: Hermann Hesse
aboutText: Hermann Hesse was a German-Swiss novelist and Nobel Prize winner. His novels Siddhartha and Steppenwolf explore themes of self-discovery and Eastern philosophy.

name: Chinua Achebe
aboutText: Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian novelist whose debut novel Things Fall Apart is the most widely read book in modern African literature, selling over 20 million copies.

name: Rumi
aboutText: Rumi was a 13th century Persian poet and Sufi mystic whose poetry transcends religion and culture. His Masnavi is considered one of the greatest works of Persian literature.

name: Anton Chekhov
aboutText: Anton Chekhov was a Russian playwright and short story writer widely regarded as one of the greatest short story writers in history.

name: James Joyce
aboutText: James Joyce was an Irish novelist considered one of the most influential writers of the 20th century. His novel Ulysses revolutionized the form of the novel.

name: Rabindranath Tagore
aboutText: Rabindranath Tagore was an Indian polymath and Nobel Prize winner who reshaped Bengali literature and music.

name: Mikhail Bulgakov
aboutText: Mikhail Bulgakov was a Soviet-era Russian writer whose masterpiece The Master and Margarita is considered one of the greatest novels of the 20th century.

name: Colleen Hoover
aboutText: Colleen Hoover is an American author known for her emotionally charged romance and new adult fiction novels. She became a publishing phenomenon through social media.

name: George R.R. Martin
aboutText: George R.R. Martin is an American novelist best known for his epic fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire, which was adapted into the HBO series Game of Thrones.

name: Jules Verne
aboutText: Jules Verne was a French novelist and pioneer of science fiction. His adventure novels including Journey to the Center of the Earth and Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea inspired generations of readers.

name: F. Scott Fitzgerald
aboutText: F. Scott Fitzgerald was an American novelist whose masterpiece The Great Gatsby is one of the greatest American novels ever written, capturing the essence of the Jazz Age.

name: John Steinbeck
aboutTitle: Voice of the American Working Class
aboutText: John Steinbeck was an American author and Nobel Prize winner. His novels The Grapes of Wrath and Of Mice and Men powerfully depict the struggles of ordinary Americans.

name: Cormac McCarthy
aboutTitle: The Dark Poet of American Fiction
aboutText: Cormac McCarthy was an American novelist known for his dark and violent depictions of the American South and West. His novels The Road and No Country for Old Men are modern classics.

name: Khaled Hosseini
aboutText: Khaled Hosseini is an Afghan-American novelist best known for The Kite Runner and A Thousand Splendid Suns, two of the most beloved novels of the 21st century.

name: Markus Zusak
aboutText: Markus Zusak is an Australian author best known for The Book Thief, a novel set in Nazi Germany narrated by Death, which has sold over 17 million copies worldwide.

name: Gillian Flynn
aboutText: Gillian Flynn is an American author known for her dark psychological thrillers. Her novel Gone Girl became a worldwide phenomenon and was adapted into a successful film.

name: Dan Brown
aboutText: Dan Brown is an American author best known for The Da Vinci Code, one of the best-selling novels of all time. His Robert Langdon series combines art history with thrilling mysteries.

name: Paulo Coelho
aboutText: Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian novelist best known for The Alchemist, one of the best-selling books in history. His works have been translated into 80 languages.

name: Naguib Mahfouz
aboutText: Naguib Mahfouz was an Egyptian writer and the first Arabic-language author to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. His Cairo Trilogy is considered the greatest work in modern Arabic literature.

name: Isabel Allende
aboutText: Isabel Allende is a Chilean-American author known for her passionate storytelling and magical realism. Her debut novel The House of the Spirits is a Latin American classic.

name: Umberto Eco
aboutText: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist and philosopher best known for The Name of the Rose, a historical murder mystery set in a medieval monastery.

name: Milan Kundera
aboutText: Milan Kundera was a Czech-French novelist best known for The Unbearable Lightness of Being, a philosophical novel exploring love, politics, and human existence.

name: Gabriel García Lorca
aboutText: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright widely considered one of the most important Spanish-language poets of the 20th century.

name: Salman Rushdie
aboutText: Salman Rushdie is a British-Indian novelist whose novel Midnight's Children won the Booker Prize. His works blend history, mythology, and magical realism.

name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
aboutText: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is a Nigerian author known for her powerful explorations of identity, gender, and culture. Her novel Americanah is a modern classic.

name: Kazuo Ishiguro
aboutText: Kazuo Ishiguro is a British-Japanese novelist and Nobel Prize winner. His novels The Remains of the Day and Never Let Me Go are masterpieces of restraint and emotional depth.

name: Jhumpa Lahiri
aboutTitle: The Voice of the Indian Diaspora
aboutText: Jhumpa Lahiri is an American author of Indian descent who won the Pulitzer Prize for her debut short story collection Interpreter of Maladies.
